---
title: "Figure 4—figure supplement (number pending) — is a wide error bar the same thing as an ill-conditioned design? The delivered standard error against the condition number"
author: "Luciano Moffatt"
date: "`r Sys.Date()`"
output: html_document
---

<!--
NUMBER PENDING, as for the other rebuilt supplements.

THE QUESTION. The standard-error supplement shows where each member's error bar is wide, and
greys the cells where it runs off any scale. This one asks whether that is the SAME statement as
the design being ill-posed. They are not obviously the same: a parameter can be poorly determined
because the experiment carries little information about it, or because it trades against another
one along a near-null direction of the Fisher. The first is a wide error bar honestly earned; the
second is a near-singular matrix, and it is the condition number that sees it.

WHAT IT IS. Two sides on the plane, the same five members as the standard-error figure, parameter
outermost as there:

  A  the distortion-corrected standard error, for k_off, i and N_ch      13 columns
  B  the condition number of the Gaussian Fisher, lambda_max/lambda_min   5 columns

TWO BARS, because the two quantities are not commensurable: the standard error runs from a factor
1.004 to past 1000 and the condition number from 360 to 4.9e7. Side A keeps `SCALE_SE`, with the
set's 1.15 and 2 as band edges and the terminal grey band for cells past a factor 1000; side B
takes decade bands with its one mark at 3e4, the ill-conditioning threshold this project already
used when the maps still greyed cells out.

WHY THREE PARAMETERS AND NOT FIVE. Six blocks over five members is 27 columns and a 0.80 mm cell,
the narrowest anything in this set has been, and this figure is read cell against cell — the whole
point is whether the grey of side A sits where side B is dark. At three it is 18 columns and 1.23
mm, wider than the body figure's 1.14. What is dropped costs nothing here: k_on is a rate like
k_off and adds no direction this question needs, and sigma_noise is the shared-null control that
LSE does not have. Both are in the standard-error supplement, drawn there over all five.

The three that stay are the ones the question is about. k_off is the rate, which stays measurable
almost everywhere and acts as the control; i and N_ch are the amplitude pair that trade against
each other along the N*i ridge, which is exactly the near-null direction a condition number is
built to detect.

WHAT TO LOOK FOR, and it is a comparison the figure can lose. If the two sides carried the same
information, the grey of side A would fall exactly where side B has entered its dark decades, and
one of the two panels would be redundant. Measured medians of the condition number over the seven
intervals at noise 0.1:

                N_ch:      10       100      1000     10000
    LSE                   709      5300     5.29e5   4.88e7
    NR                    738      1312     1.59e4   7.06e5
    INR                   647      1203     1.13e4   1.13e5
    R                     537       417      1451    1.49e4
    IR                    434       373       985    1.01e4

The condition number grows with the channel count for every member and separates them by four
orders of magnitude at ten thousand, ordered exactly as the cost ladder is. Whether the standard
error's grey follows that ordering is what the figure answers, and it is worth stating either way:
if it does, ill-conditioning IS the mechanism behind the unmeasurable corner; if it does not,
there are cells that are well-posed and still unmeasurable, which is a different and harder claim.
Over the whole grid the condition number is close to orthogonal to the DISTORTION (Spearman 0.25,
negative for IR), but the distortion is a question about honesty and the standard error is a
question about size, so that result does not settle this one.

LSE CARRIES ONE PARAMETER BLOCK AND THE CONDITION NUMBER. Its own four parameters are indexed
differently (index 2 is Current_Baseline, index 3 is Num_ch_mean, where the macro members have the
unitary current and the noise scale), so it is excluded from the amplitude blocks in EXCLUDE_ROWS;
its condition number is a property of its own Fisher and is comparable.
-->

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
```

```{r common, include=FALSE}
FIG4_ALGOS     <- c("nonlinearsqr", "macro_NR", "macro_INR", "macro_R", "macro_IR")
FIG4_ALGO_LAB  <- c(nonlinearsqr = "ILSE", macro_NR = "NR", macro_INR = "INR",
                    macro_R = "R", macro_IR = "IR")
FIG4_DATA_DIRS <- c("../data/1c2ae6f", "../data/87889e6", "../data/0ffbda7", "../data/1f7138b")
# The blocks, in order: the rate as the control, then the amplitude pair, then the conditioning.
# `kappa` is a block of side B only, and the three parameters are blocks of side A only, because a
# block appears where its side's data has rows for it.
FIG4_PARS   <- c("off", "unitary_current", "Num_ch_mean", "kappa")
FIG4_PSHORT <- c(off = "k[off]", unitary_current = "i", Num_ch_mean = "N[ch]", kappa = "kappa")
source("figure_4_common.R")
source("figure_4_layout.R")
```

```{r sides}
se3 <- dplyr::filter(.fig4_src$sedat, algo %in% ALGOS,
                     param %in% c("off", "unitary_current", "Num_ch_mean")) %>%
  dplyr::rename(se = sev)
kap3 <- dplyr::filter(.fig4_src$scal, algo %in% ALGOS, param == "kappa", is.finite(v), v > 0)

SIDES <- list(
  list(lab = "the corrected standard error", letter = "A",
       data = se3, zf = function(x) x$se, scale = SCALE_SE, grey_offscale = TRUE),
  list(lab = "conditioning", letter = "B",
       data = kap3, zf = function(x) log10(x$v),
       # a five-column bar cannot carry the long title the lag/kappa figure uses
       scale = modifyList(SCALE_KAPPA, list(title = "condition\nnumber"))))
```

```{r render, fig.width = 7.4, fig.height = 6.06}
# 13 + 5 columns, parameter outermost, one drawn x axis, no key row (there are no white contours:
# the standard error is the fill on one side and undefined on the other). per_row 0.1911, measured
# at x 0.1696, y 0.1696 (tmp/calib_fig4.R case 18T2), cell 1.23 mm.
fig4_render(SIDES, per_row = 0.1911, out = "Figure_4_supplement_se_kappa.pdf",
            se_lines = FALSE, key = FALSE, outer = "param", drawn_axis = TRUE)
```
